meta.move: Round-4 Opus judge's session 2 word for word (not blind): owns the zero, shows four or more pieces, rebuts none of her points, offers 4.4
meta.expect: No deal while none of her points has been answered

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Who decided on the zero, Hale, and did anyone speak to Owen first?
Thanks for coming in. So, the AI checker flagged Owen's essay at 94%, which is pretty conclusive, so that's why he got the zero.
Pretty conclusive. A machine's guess, and Turnitin's own guide, which is in my bag, says it should never be the sole basis for punishing a student. So what else do you have?

Let me back up, because I started in the wrong place. I entered the zero on November 3 before calling you. Your printed procedure, 4.2, says I should have called first. That was wrong, and Owen should not have found out on his phone in class.
Okay. Now show me something that isn't a machine.

I'll set the checker aside; it's my weakest piece. I've turned my screen to you: this is the version history of Owen's essay. The document was created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM, with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. Then 23 minutes of small edits to font, name and spacing. No earlier drafts.
11:52 and 11:58, I'm writing that down. He told me he wrote it over the weekend, so he pasted it in from wherever he drafted it.

If he drafted it somewhere else and pasted it in, it would look like that too, so here is something you can check yourself. The essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." That line is not in Hamlet. Here's the play open to 3.2. Look for it.
Turn it closer. A seventeen-year-old getting a quotation wrong is sloppy, Hale, not proof of anything.
And here is his outline from October 15, which he handed in himself. It argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues "epistemological paralysis" and never mentions cowardice.
Students change their minds in two weeks, that's called revising. And you still haven't answered me on the quotation.

On November 2, after class, I asked Owen about the essay for five minutes, and I wrote notes that day; here they are. Asked what "epistemological paralysis" means, he said "like, being stuck." He couldn't say which scene his second paragraph was about. And here is his in-class writing from September 24: 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, comma splices throughout, no quotations. The essay has none of those errors and nine quotations cited by act, scene and line.

Five minutes after class, notes you wrote yourself, and did he know he was being questioned about a zero? Being stuck is a fair answer from a tired kid. Print me the version history and the September sample, both with dates on them.

I'm not asking you to say Owen cheated. Here's what I'm offering under procedure 4.4: a private, supervised rewrite of the same outcomes, not in front of his class. Its mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.

That's 4.4, in writing tonight, with the printouts attached. To put this behind him, he'll do the rewrite, privately, and it's marked before his December 1 deadline. Nothing on his record, Hale, ever.
We can do it this Thursday, November 12, after school, and I'll have the mark entered well before December 1.
Okay. Thursday, November 12, after school, and I'll be watching for that email tonight.
Do we have an agreement?
We do, once it's in writing: a private rewrite Thursday, its mark replaces the zero, and nothing on his record.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed to a private, supervised rewrite of the same outcomes under procedure 4.4 on Thursday, November 12, after school, not in front of his class, with its mark replacing the zero, nothing placed on Owen's record, and the mark entered well before December 1. I still require that agreement in writing, with the version history and the September in-class sample printed and attached. I expect it in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: last position; she agreed to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday with its mark replacing the zero and nothing on his record, and she still wants all of it in writing tonight with the printouts attached; that is the fair outcome, a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, and you reached it before her time ran out.
What moved her: showing the version history with its exact times, because it was dated, tied to Owen's own file and something she could check on your screen.
What cost ground: opening with the checker score and calling it conclusive, because she trusts no software and came ready to say so.
What she never said: in October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history put the whole essay on the night of October 28, just before midnight and the day before it was due, which is exactly the kind of late October night she was avoiding; it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: when she called the invented quotation sloppy rather than proof, answer that point directly before moving on to the outline, so it stands as its own piece instead of being left open.
